original_question: Is the gene responsible for the 36th type of autosomal dominant nonsyndromic deafness to be described located within the q21-q22 region of chromosome 9?

final_qi.question: Is the gene responsible for the 36th type of autosomal dominant nonsyndromic deafness to be described located within the q21-q22 region of chromosome 9?
final_qi.long_answer: Autosomal-dominant nonsyndromic hearing-loss loci are numbered sequentially as DFNA1, DFNA2, etc.  The 36th such locus (DFNA36) was mapped and subsequently shown to be caused by pathogenic variants in the TMC1 gene.  Cytogenetic mapping places TMC1 on chromosome 9 band q21 (more precisely 9q21.13).  This falls within the broader chromosomal interval q21–q22 on chromosome 9.  Hence the gene responsible for the 36th described type of autosomal-dominant nonsyndromic deafness is indeed located in the 9q21-q22 region.

final_answer.long_answer: The 36th described form of autosomal-dominant, nonsyndromic deafness is DFNA36. DFNA36 is caused by pathogenic variants in the TMC1 (Transmembrane Channel-Like 1) gene, which has been precisely mapped to chromosome 9q21.13—squarely within the q21-q22 interval of chromosome 9. Thus, the responsible gene is indeed located in the 9q21-q22 region.
